sources.title: Wikipedia: Convention on the Rights of the Child

sections.body: In 1989 the United Nations agreed the Convention on the Rights of the Child. Almost every country in the world has signed it.
It says every child has rights, including the right to education, health care, play, safety, a name and nationality, and to be heard.
Rights come with responsibilities: respecting other people's rights too.
The Convention is the most widely ratified human rights treaty in history.

quiz.q: Which is a right in the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child?
options: The right to stay up all night
hints: Rights are about what every child needs to grow up well.
The right to health care is in the Convention. Which option is also about a basic need?
quiz.explain: Every child has the right to education.

quiz.q: What responsibility comes with having rights?
hints: If you have rights, so does everyone else.
How should you treat others' rights?
If you have the right to be heard, others also have the right to be heard. What does that mean you should do?
quiz.explain: We should respect other people's rights as well as our own.

quiz.q: Who does the UN Convention say has these rights?
options: Only children who go to school
hints: Do these rights depend on where you live?
Almost all countries signed it, rich and poor.
Example: a rule that all cyclists must wear helmets covers each cyclist, not just some.
quiz.explain: The Convention says every child has rights, wherever they live. Going to school is one of those rights, not a test for getting them.
